identification.summary: Carmine Tsunami is Microsoft's name for a private sector offensive actor (PSOA), formerly tracked as DEV-0196, which Microsoft links with high confidence to the Israel-based vendor QuaDream and its mobile spyware platform sold to governments [S1]. Microsoft says it develops KingsPawn, iOS malware strongly linked to QuaDream, and operates an access-as-a-service model, selling exploitation services and malware without conducting targeting itself [S1]. QuaDream was incorporated in Israel in August 2016 and has no website [S1].
identification.firstObserved: QuaDream incorporated August 2016 [S1]. Exploit and spyware activity against victims is dated by reporting to 2021 [S2][S3]. Microsoft published DEV-0196 findings on 2023-04-11 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Carmine Tsunami (formerly DEV-0196), renamed in April 2023 under its taxonomy [S1]. Product names differ by source: Microsoft calls the malware KingsPawn, Citizen Lab calls the exploit ENDOFDAYS, and QuaDream's platform is called REIGN; Microsoft assesses with medium confidence that KingsPawn is part of the system publicly discussed as REIGN [S1][S2]. Do not merge with Caramel Tsunami (SOURGUM, DevilsTongue/Candiru), a separate Microsoft-tracked PSOA [S1]. Reporting of QuaDream's closure is by an Israeli business outlet citing unnamed sources [S5].

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor is identified in the sources. Microsoft describes a commercial vendor selling to government customers [S1]. Reporting names Saudi Arabia and Ghana among alleged clients (Microsoft cites Haaretz, which could not confirm a Ghana election allegation) [S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft: high confidence that DEV-0196 is linked to QuaDream; high confidence in the access-as-a-service model and that KingsPawn was developed by DEV-0196 and strongly linked to QuaDream; medium confidence that the malware is part of REIGN [S1].
attribution.basis: Microsoft analysis of samples and infrastructure, in coordination with Citizen Lab findings [S1][S2]; Reuters 2022 sourcing on QuaDream's iPhone exploit capability [S3]; Meta's December 2022 removal of QuaDream-associated accounts [S1][S4].

objectives: Commercial: develop and sell exploits, spyware and supporting infrastructure to government customers for covert device surveillance [S1]. Observed victims were civil society members, including journalists, political opposition figures and an NGO worker [S1][S2].

regions: Victims in North America, Central Asia, Southeast Asia, Europe and the Middle East [S1]
Operator-linked infrastructure in Bulgaria, Czechia, Hungary, Ghana, Israel, Mexico, Romania, Singapore, UAE and Uzbekistan (per Citizen Lab, as cited by Microsoft) [S1]
targeting.notes: At least five civil society victims were identified by Citizen Lab [S1][S2]. Customers, not the vendor, select targets [S1]. No military or DoD-specific targeting is reported in the sources gathered.

capabilities.summary: KingsPawn targets iOS 14 primarily, with indications some code could run on Android; Microsoft assesses newer iOS versions were likely targeted by updated variants [S1]. It has a monitor agent (Objective-C) and a main agent (Go) [S1]. The monitor agent deletes forensic artifacts and manages child processes to avoid crash artifacts [S1]. The main agent collects device and network information, retrieves files, uses the camera in the background, tracks location, monitors calls, accesses the keychain and generates iCloud TOTP codes [S1]. Evasion includes injection into tccd to bypass camera and microphone consent prompts, use of mediaserverd for background execution, PMAP, AMFI and sandbox escape bypasses, a nested app extension for hidden XPC messaging, and masquerading as Apple binaries [S1]. Citizen Lab named the zero-click exploit ENDOFDAYS, which reportedly used invisible iCloud calendar invitations [S2]. Reuters (Feb 2022) reported QuaDream gained a remote iPhone exploit in 2021 relying on the same Apple flaw as NSO's FORCEDENTRY (CVE-2021-30860); Microsoft did not confirm this link [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: QuaDream incorporated
campaigns.summary: QuaDream incorporated in Israel; Reuters reporting names founders as a former Israeli military official and two former NSO employees.

campaigns.name: Exploitation of civil society victims
campaigns.summary: Citizen Lab reporting, as relayed by secondary coverage, dates ENDOFDAYS use against iOS 14.4 and 14.4.2 to 2021; Apple notified affected individuals in 2021.

campaigns.name: Reuters report on QuaDream iPhone tool
campaigns.summary: Reuters reports QuaDream developed a remote iPhone exploit in 2021 similar to NSO's FORCEDENTRY-based capability.

campaigns.name: Meta removes QuaDream-linked accounts
campaigns.summary: Meta's threat report removed about 250 accounts linked to QuaDream.

campaigns.name: Microsoft and Citizen Lab disclosure
campaigns.summary: Microsoft publishes DEV-0196/KingsPawn analysis and IOCs; Citizen Lab reports at least five civil society victims across multiple regions.

campaigns.name: Reported QuaDream shutdown
campaigns.summary: Calcalist reports, via unnamed sources, that QuaDream is shutting down and laying off staff after the disclosures.

diamond.adversary: Commercial vendor QuaDream (Israel) operating as an access-as-a-service provider; customer governments direct targeting [S1].
diamond.capability: KingsPawn iOS spyware (Objective-C monitor agent, Go main agent), ENDOFDAYS zero-click calendar-invite exploit, anti-forensics [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Domains from commodity registrars and cheap cloud hosts accepting cryptocurrency, typically one domain per IP, Let's Encrypt or self-signed certificates resembling Kubernetes deployments, country-specific TLDs or target-themed names [S1].
diamond.victim: Journalists, political opposition figures and NGO workers across North America, Central Asia, Southeast Asia, Europe and the Middle East [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Part of the commercial spyware market sold to governments; Meta, Microsoft and Citizen Lab exposure was followed by reported closure [S1][S4][S5].
diamond.technology: Apple iOS devices (iOS 14 primarily), iCloud calendar and messaging attack surface; Lockdown Mode and prompt updates are Microsoft's mitigations [S1].

gaps: Citizen Lab's primary report could not be opened (host unreachable); its findings are cited through Microsoft and secondary coverage [S1][S2].
Reuters and Calcalist primary articles were not fetched; Reuters and closure claims rest on search-result summaries [S3][S5].
Whether KingsPawn exploited FORCEDENTRY or a different flaw is unconfirmed; Microsoft did not confirm the Reuters claim [S1].
Customer identities are unconfirmed; Haaretz alleged clients that Microsoft relays but Haaretz could not fully verify [S1].
Current status after the reported 2023 shutdown, including successor firms or reuse of tooling, is not established in sources gathered.
Secondary sources differ on affected iOS range; Microsoft states iOS 14 primarily [S1][S2].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is personal and official iOS devices of staff, contractors and partners, plus iCloud services. STEP 2: Commercial vendors provide zero-click capability to customers lacking in-house skill, widening the pool of actors able to reach iPhones; observed victims were civil society, not military [S1]. STEP 3: Template is zero-click delivery, privilege and sandbox bypass, background camera, microphone and location collection, then anti-forensic cleanup [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is that this vendor's tooling is no longer actively sold given the reported shutdown, with similar PSOA capability reused by other customers [S5]. MDCOA is an equivalent zero-click iOS capability used against deployed personnel, journalists or coalition-partner officials. Candidate indicators: Microsoft-published file paths such as the staging subridged binary and fud.appex, com.apple.avcapture, and listed domains [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track PSOA disclosures from Microsoft and Citizen Lab and mobile-device indicators for personnel in travel or deployment status. (2) Authorities: personal-device inspection and monitoring raise legal questions; confirm authority and privacy rules before collection. (3) Mission assurance: enforce device updates, Lockdown Mode for high-risk users and device compartmentation. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partners and counterintelligence, and treat victim notification such as Apple's as a trigger for incident response [S1][S2].
